Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: service-startup failures in isvc-api in us-central1. Multiple hosts failing health checks due to KMS signing errors (504/429). Paging on-call: @Megan (eng-oncall)

Megan (eng-oncall): seeing spike in KMS latency. Startup logs show repeated `gcp-kms: request timeout` and `signing failed: 504` during instance init. Rolling restarts failing L7 health checks.

Megan (eng-oncall): @Raj can you confirm if this is regional (us-central1) only or global?

Raj (sre): I'm seeing similar errors forwarded from our KMS proxy metrics — 429s then 5xx from KMS control plane. Errors started ~1905001200. Cloud KMS graph shows throttling spikes and elevated p99 latency. No active config change from our side.

Megan (eng-oncall): customer impact = service startup failures for dedicated/private deployments in us-central1; some hosted customers affected briefly during autoscale. Escalating to P1.

OpsPager: @Aaron has been notified (pager duty).

Aaron (eng-runtime): I'm in. Attaching a few log snippets from failing init: ```
[init] 2026-05-12T12:07:21Z signing: request to kms.googleapis.com/v1/projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/...: context deadline exceeded
[init] 2026-05-12T12:07:22Z auth: received 429 Too Many Requests from KMS
[health] 2026-05-12T12:07:30Z health check failed: unable to sign startup token
```

Aaron (eng-runtime): Quick ask: can we enable local cached signing for warm pools as fallback? If we can flip a flag to use cached service account tokens temporarily it would let instances come up.

Raj (sre): We should avoid long-lived keys. Proposal: fallback to short-lived cached JWTs with conservative TTL (5m) on warm pool only, not full production path. I can prepare a rollout if product approves.

Megan (eng-oncall): @Lisa can you confirm whether Support is receiving customer tickets? Need timeline for comms.

Lisa (support): yep, two customers reported failed feature launches in us-central1 within last 12m. Triage notes: errors surfaced as 500s in client logs referencing "signing error". Creating status page draft.

Incident Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0512-KMS-THROTTLE. Priority: P1. Lead: Megan (eng-oncall).

Aaron (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigations I'm implementing now: 1) increase local retry/backoff up to 10s with jitter for KMS calls, 2) route startup signing to secondary region KMS (us-east1) for new instances while we investigate, 3) avoid full restart waves until warmed instances are validated. Rolling change to runtime config in progress (canary 1 host).

Megan (eng-oncall): Confirm when canary is up. If canary succeeds we'll do staged rollout across warm pool.

Aaron (eng-runtime): Canary passed (single host) at 1905001450. Startup succeeded using secondary KMS endpoint. No client-visible degradation on canary.

Raj (sre): Reaching out to GCP support now (case created). Attaching KMS request IDs and latency traces. Also enabling additional logging on KMS proxy (sampling 100%).

Lisa (support): Status page update ready (draft): "We're investigating increased latency and errors from Cloud KMS impacting service startup in us-central1. Engineers are actively mitigating by routing signing to a secondary region and adjusting retries. We will provide updates every 15 minutes." Asking for approval to publish.

Megan (eng-oncall): Publish the draft. Add note: customers with dedicated warm pools may see delayed scaling until mitigation finishes.

Aaron (eng-runtime): Rolling to 40% of warm pool now (1905001600). Observed error rate down ~80% for startup signing calls. CPU/memory stable.

Raj (sre): GCP replied: they have an ongoing control plane issue causing elevated 429s in us-central1 for KMS; mitigation in progress on their side. ETA unknown. They've requested request IDs and traces (provided).

Megan (eng-oncall): Next steps: keep routing startup signing to secondary region for new instances, continue staged rollout, avoid full restarts, monitor for auth/regression. Prepare post-incident RCA for dedicated customers.

Lisa (support): Running list of affected customers attached in internal ticket. Will notify enterprise contacts after we have timeline for resolution and rollback plan.

Aaron (eng-runtime): Note: we also introduced a temporary circuit-breaker that will short-circuit signing calls after 6 retries to avoid excessive queueing. Monitoring to ensure no data corruption.

Megan (eng-oncall): On-call handoff to Raj at 1905001800 for monitoring overnight. I will brief morning shift and start RCA doc.

Raj (sre): Taking handoff. I'll watch the KMS proxy dashboards and error budgets. If GCP reports resolution we'll schedule gradual rollback to normal routing with canary.

Incident Bot: Incident status update: mitigations in place (secondary KMS routing + retries). Impact reduced. Next update at +15m.

Megan (eng-oncall): Thanks team. Keep notes in the incident doc and add any customer comms drafts there.

(End of thread)
